translated: I've already talked quite a bit, but I'd like for us to take a look at the card illustrations together.
Someone said they could feel the emotions through the changes in Saki's tone of voice.
Thank you so much.
I'm so happy that everyone understands it so well.
It's hard to put into words, but I feel like I was really able to face Saki head-on.
This story made me feel like the way I've faced her until now has finally taken shape.
So, before we look at the illustrations in detail, the illustration production team
sent in some comments about the outfits, so I'd like to introduce those.
Regarding the design...
As Leo/need grows, they find themselves unable to deliver music to the fans close to them.
The story follows Saki as she realizes she wants to keep playing the free, intimate music she always has.
The overall motif is an adventurer traveling and observing the stars, representing their journey so far and where they are now.
We used a blue and yellow gradient for Ichika and Honami.
This represents the dawn breaking, which symbolizes the image of Leo/need changing.
What a lovely comment.
Thank you very much.
For Saki alone, we didn't use a gradient, but used yellow on the surface of the cloak covering her body.
This is meant to express how she is hiding her true feelings.
Wait, really?
We have to see this.
I want to actually look at the illustrations now and talk about them.
Aren't they incredibly beautiful?
They really are amazing.
I was just talking with the staff about it. They look like something out of a movie or a picture book.
And look, her hair is short!
Let's take a look.
Ta-da!
